## What The Business Is

CoreWeave is an AI-focused cloud infrastructure company, listed on Nasdaq as CRWV in March 2025, that sells access to high-performance GPU compute and related cloud services to AI labs, hyperscalers, startups, and enterprises. Management describes it as “The Essential Cloud for AI,” positioned between model developers and silicon suppliers by delivering infrastructure, software, and technical expertise for building and running AI at scale. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/))

## What It Does

CoreWeave rents and operates accelerated compute capacity built around NVIDIA GPUs, plus supporting CPU, storage, networking, inference, orchestration, and developer-tooling layers. The transcript emphasizes a shift from “just GPUs” toward an integrated AI cloud platform: customers use CoreWeave for training, inference, agentic workloads, cross-cloud connectivity, flexible reservations, spot capacity, dedicated inference, and Weights & Biases tooling. In Q1 2026, the company said over 90% of reserved-instance customers used at least two products, and it highlighted products such as Flex Reservations, Spot, Dedicated Inference, CoreWeave ARENA, and W&B Weave / W&B Models. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Q1 2026 showed very large demand and scale expansion: revenue was $2.078 billion, up from $982 million a year earlier; adjusted EBITDA was $1.157 billion; revenue backlog reached $99.4 billion; and active power surpassed 1 GW, with contracted power above 3.5 GW after adding more than 400 MW in the quarter. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/))

Customer momentum was broad in the last 90 days: CoreWeave reported multiple new Meta agreements, including a new $21 billion commitment signed in March, a multi-year Anthropic agreement to support Claude development and deployment, and expanded relationships with Cohere, Jane Street, and Mistral. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/)) Jane Street also committed about $6 billion to use CoreWeave’s AI cloud and made a $1 billion equity investment at $109 per Class A share. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/Jane-Street-Signs-6-Billion-AI-Cloud-Agreement-With-CoreWeave/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))

Financing access improved despite the capital intensity: CoreWeave closed a $3.1 billion delayed-draw term loan facility in May 2026, saying the deal was oversubscribed, priced at SOFR + 4.50%, and brought year-to-date debt/equity capital secured to more than $20 billion. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Closes-3-1-Billion-Loan-Facility-Expanding-Access-to-Public-Markets-for-GPU-Backed-Financing/default.aspx)) Technology-wise, CoreWeave announced an industry-first bring-up and validation of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 with Dell, reinforcing its positioning near the leading edge of AI infrastructure. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Completes-Industry-First-Bring-Up-and-Validation-of-NVIDIA-Vera-Rubin-NVL72/default.aspx))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

The business remains highly capital intensive and loss-making on GAAP metrics. In Q1 2026, CoreWeave reported a $144 million operating loss, $536 million of net interest expense, a $740 million net loss, and an adjusted net loss of $589 million; current debt was $7.547 billion and non-current debt was $17.312 billion at March 31, 2026. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/))

Funding needs continue: in June 2026, CoreWeave priced $1.25 billion of 9.625% senior notes due 2032 and €2 billion of 8.500% senior notes due 2032, with proceeds intended for general corporate purposes including repayment of indebtedness. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Announces-Pricing-of-1-25-Billion-of-Senior-Notes-and-2-Billion-of-Senior-Notes/default.aspx)) This underscores dependence on debt and capital markets to keep converting backlog into live capacity.

Customer concentration and competitive risk remain important. CoreWeave’s own risk language cites potential disruption in strategic relationships, third-party providers, suppliers, data-center partners, financial performance, capital requirements, and ability to raise capital. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/)) A July 2026 report that Meta may rent out its own AI compute pressured neocloud stocks, with CoreWeave reportedly falling 10.8%, because such a move could make a key customer a future competitor or reduce longer-term reliance on external GPU-cloud suppliers. ([tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/meta-reportedly-plans-to-rent-out-its-ai-compute?utm_source=openai))

## Bull Case
- $99.4B revenue backlog, Meta's $21B commitment, Anthropic, and Jane Street's $6B deal (plus $1B equity at $109/share) validate demand far ahead of deployed capacity (1 GW active vs. 3.5 GW contracted).
- Revenue more than doubled YoY ($2.08B in Q1 2026, ~$8B+ annualized run-rate exiting the year) with strong adjusted EBITDA ($1.16B in Q1), showing unit economics work as capacity comes online.
- Capital markets remain open despite the burn: >$20B of debt/equity secured YTD 2026, an oversubscribed $3.1B term loan, and GPU-backed financing structures. First-mover Vera Rubin NVL72 validation keeps CoreWeave at the leading edge.
- In a bull scenario, the market values the backlog conversion and awards an EV well above today's, pushing market cap toward $60–70B.

## Bear Case
- GAAP economics are poor: Q1 2026 operating loss of $144M, $536M net interest expense, $740M net loss. TTM FCF is -$10.6B and worsening as capex scales.
- Debt load is heavy (~$24.9B total) and expensive — new notes priced at 9.6% USD / 8.5% EUR — so equity value is highly leveraged to execution and rates.
- Customer concentration risk is acute: the July 2026 Meta compute-rental report knocked the stock ~11% in a day; a key customer becoming a competitor could impair backlog value.
- In a bear scenario, funding stress or backlog doubts compress EV toward or below current levels; after the ~$32B EV–market-cap gap, equity could fall to $30–35B.

## Logic
1. **Forward FCF:** TTM FCF is -$10.6B. Capex is accelerating (400+ MW added in Q1 alone, >$20B capital raised YTD to fund buildout), only partly offset by rising operating cash flow from EBITDA growth. I project 12-month forward FCF of approximately **-$14,000M**.
2. **Applied multiple:** Current EV/FCF is ~-7.3x (EV $77.7B / FCF -$10.6B); the 1y average FCF/EV yield is ~-10.7%. Because the deepening burn is contracted growth investment backed by a $99.4B backlog, I apply a slightly less negative **EV/FCF of -6.0x** (the market pays more EV per dollar of growth-driven burn, consistent with the improving 1y vs. current yield trend).
3. **Forward EV:** -$14,000M × -6.0 = **$84,000M**.
4. **Bridge to market cap:** Current EV ($77,697.5M) minus current market cap ($45,571.5M) = **$32,126M** net-debt gap. Holding the gap constant: $84,000M − $32,126M ≈ **$51,874M** forward market cap (~14% above current), within one standard deviation of the 3y market-cap history ($50.5B mean, $14.8B std).
